patriotic romance in the idea of a building which had failed at last;

castle, the last of its dynasty, with its broken towers and its

more you look at the thing, the more you can see what is wrong with it.

architecture is out of date. This is one of those ages when the world
is turning upside down. Men have grown too tall; too tall for the old
buildings. The towers tower up to heaven.

prompt: Write a passage arguing that superficial appreciation of a culture's artistic or social expressions without understanding its underlying values is problematic.

But the real danger of such a superficial
appreciation lies in this: that it does not merely leave us cold, it
actually turns us cold with our own coldness. We do not feel so much
that we are ignorant; we really do feel that we are insane. We do not
feel that we have missed some vital truth; we feel that we have lost
some vital senses. We are like men who cannot see any colours except

prompt: Write a personal essay that revisits a place from your past, comparing how it appears now with your memories of it from years ago.
completion:
I have no more idea what I can do for England than when I was a small
boy, when I did not know any better. I only feel that England is
doubtless in some degree in danger and I should like to be of help if
only I could find out what sort of help I can give. But I cannot help
thinking that this is the best part of the country; that this is the
part which is most untouched by modern civilization, and therefore the
most hopeful. The fact that the sea is so blue here seems to me like
the fact that there are flowers on earth. The fact that the sky is so
high and clear seems to me like the fact that there are sunsets. The
fact that the sea has such an awful roar and the sky such an awful
whisper, seems to me like the fact that there are storms and thunder
bolts. All that I can say is that I wish all men could see what I see.
It is not only a beautiful place, it is also a sane one. The sea, the
sky, the land--all these things are sane. They do not pretend to be
something else. They do not hide themselves behind a veil. They are
not pretending to be something that they are not. The sky does not
pretend to be a blue sky. It is a blue sky. The sea does not pretend
to be the sea. It is the sea. I think that England ought to be like
this. I think England ought to look like this. I do not mean merely
that England ought to be beautiful; I mean that it ought to look
beautiful. I do not mean merely that England ought to be sane; I mean
that it ought to look sane. If you cannot see a thing, then you cannot
think it.

completion:

love thee more than ever,” it is difficult to think that he could be
treated with indifference, and still less with contempt. But there
are two great ways in which even very deep emotional commitments may
be betrayed by what we call fidelity. It may mean being indifferent.
It may mean being contemptuous.

If you say to a man, “I will love thee more than ever,” and he says,
“Good gracious! do, then,” you are, in truth, betrayed into
contempt—into the contempt of a child. If you say to a man, “I will
love thee more than ever,” and he says, “That’s all right;” you are
betrayed into indifference—into the indifference of a dog.

But there is also the more serious way in which a man may betray his
friend through the mere fact that he does not really believe in
friendship. A friend, when you have been faithful to him for a long
time, is like your father. He has not only a claim upon you, but a
claim of some sort upon you. But this claim comes to an end when you
have made him a martyr. Then he is no longer your father, but merely a
man whom you have made an enemy. He was your father because you owed
him the duty of loving him. But now you have given yourself the
duty of hating him. That is how the matter stands.

prompt: Write an analytical paragraph distinguishing between two different types of criticism that might be directed at popular media or cultural phenomena.

The first type of criticism is simply a criticism of the thing itself.

for being a mere titillating sensation. But it does not attack it for

personally am always more or less inclined to prefer. The second kind

comic spirit, then, is the spiritual basis of religion, the basis which
makes us believe in a God. If the comic spirit is merely accidental

infallible proof of him.
